target.title: feat(tencent): add Tencent Hy3 provider (TokenHub and TokenPlan)
target.body:
Closes #99069

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach the current-generation Hunyuan `hy3` model or the TokenPlan endpoint. The plugin only wired `hy3-preview` on TokenHub, so onboarding (`openclaw onboard --auth-choice ...`), the provider catalog, config resolution, and docs all had no path to the `hy3` model on either endpoint, or to the TokenPlan endpoint at all. Anyone with a `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` or wanting `hy3` had no supported way to configure it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a second provider id `tencent-tokenplan` alongside the existing `tencent-tokenhub`, expands the catalog, and wires auth / onboarding / reasoning-effort end-to-end so both endpoints are first-class:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub` (existing), `tencent-tokenplan` (new)
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview` (existing), `hy3` (new)
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TENCENT_TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding flags: `--auth-choice tencent-tokenhub-api-key`, `--auth-choice tencent-tokenplan-api-key`

Non-goals: no core changes; TokenHub behavior for existing `hy3-preview` users is preserved (same env var, same onboarding flag, same default reasoning effort).

## User Impact

- Users can now select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan via `openclaw onboard` and via `openclaw.json` config.
- `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` is recognized out of the box; no manual config surgery required.
- Reasoning effort for `hy3` defaults to `high` and can be overridden to `none`; `hy3-preview` keeps its full `none` / `low` / `medium` / `high` range.
- Existing `tencent-tokenhub` + `hy3-preview` users see no behavior change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test:extension tencent` — 9/9 pass, including reasoning-effort injection for `hy3` (default `high`, override to `none` / `high`) and `hy3-preview` default behavior.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — clean.
- `pnpm test:extensions:package-boundary` — passes for all 116 plugins (tencent included).
- `pnpm lint` — 0 warnings, 0 errors across `core` / `extensions` / `scripts` shards.

Docs updated in the same commit:

- `docs/providers/tencent.md` — provider table, auth env vars, reasoning-effort matrix
- `docs/plugins/reference/tencent.md` — models / auth reference
- `docs/providers/index.md`, `docs/plugins/plugin-inventory.md` — index entries
